message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where it lives |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your local terminal (or Cloud Shell) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, your own script) |

> ⚠️ *Google Cloud does not have “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the equivalent service is “Compute Engine.”*

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1. Pick a name, zone, and machine type that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # e.g. us-central1-a, europe-west4-b, etc.
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
    --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: run a script at boot
```

### Notes

| Parameter | Meaning | Typical Value |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU | `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1` |
| `--image-family` | OS image family | `ubuntu-2004-lts` |
| `--image-project` | Project that hosts the image | `ubuntu-os-cloud` |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk | `50GB` (adjust) |
| `--boot-disk-type` | Disk type | `pd-standard` (SSD: `pd-ssd`) |
| `--metadata-from-file` | Optional startup script | `startup.sh` |

> 👉 **Prerequisites**  
> • Enable the Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> • Set the active project (`gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID`).  
> • Ensure you have the necessary IAM permissions (e.g., `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`).  

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a custom tool), here’s the minimal JSON payload you’d POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "preemptible": false
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-0"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
# Example with curl (replace placeholders)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

curl -X POST "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @instance.json
```

> 👉 **Prerequisites**  
> • OAuth 2.0 token with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
> • Compute Engine API enabled.  
> • IAM role `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (or equivalent).

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API |
| ✅ | Set default project & zone |
| ✅ | Choose a machine type that supports GPUs |
| ✅ | Specify `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator |
| ✅ | Use `ubuntu-2004-lts` image family |
| ✅ | Allocate enough boot‑disk space |
| ✅ | Grant yourself `compute.instanceAdmin.v1` permission |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-demo@YOUR_INSTANCE_IP
nvidia-smi
```

That should show the RTX A6000 GPU and its driver version. Happy computing!
